clue.text: Story-teller fell mum at last

parts.note: fell as an adjective means fierce or cruel, so grim

indicators.note: at last asks for only the closing letter of the word mum

explanation.surface: A narrator falls silent when the tale finally ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' reads as a verb but is the old adjective meaning fierce. The Brothers GRIMM collected fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm were the German collectors of folk tales, hence a story-teller.

clue.text: Go grey with worry about Herbert's plan

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
worry suggests these letters agitated into another order

parts.note: A. P. Herbert, humorist and MP, signed himself APH

explanation.surface: Anxiety turns someone's hair grey over a writer's scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with worry' rearranges GO GREY to GEOGRY, and 'about' puts APH inside. 'plan' means the lie of the land, as in the geography of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The layout or arrangement of a place, as in a building's geography, is its plan.

clue.text: In Parliament I raised this war history

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the words read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An MP brings up a war history in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DAIL and I together upwards. The Dail Eireann is Ireland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem tells of the Trojan War, so it is a history of that war.

clue.text: Tend, given office, to assume title

indicators.note: assume means take on, so the title takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Mister is a title before a man's name
a party given office is in power, so in

explanation.surface: A newly appointed official takes up a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to assume' is the container signal: the title takes the office word inside it. The surface pushes a government minister, but the definition is the verb, to tend.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to attend to their needs, a synonym of tend.

clue.text: One not getting audition for Lear — pride took a fall

indicators.note: taking a fall suggests the letters of these two words tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical tale: pride comes before a fall when someone misses the King Lear audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took a fall' rearranges LEAR and PRIDE. 'audition' is not a theatre tryout here but the act of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person, who cannot hear, follows speech by watching the mouth instead.

clue.text: Physician moderately 16?

definitions.meaning: St ... the evangelist was a doctor
the answer to 16 across is warm, and this old word means tepid, as in lukewarm

explanation.surface: A doctor who is only moderately keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is WARM; 'luke' is an old word for tepid, surviving in lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul calls the evangelist the beloved physician, and the dialect adjective means tepid, as in lukewarm.

clue.text: Current collector of copying equipment

definitions.meaning: the hinged arm on a tram or electric train roof that picks up power from overhead wires
a jointed drawing instrument that copies a figure to a different scale

explanation.surface: Someone collects old copying machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector' suggests a hobbyist, but it is a device collecting electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The same jointed lattice shape serves both as a train's overhead power pickup and as a draughtsman's scaling copier.

clue.text: Embarrassing situation arising — I'm God

indicators.note: in a down clue arising reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: being in a hole is being in an awkward fix

explanation.surface: Someone in an awkward spot declares themselves divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns HOLE to ELOH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Hebrew name for the deity used in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Hill that's Scots — or Scotus? How silly!

parts.note: John Duns Scotus was the medieval Scottish philosopher
silly or senseless means inane

explanation.surface: A scornful remark on mixing up Scots with the philosopher Scotus.
explanation.walkthrough: Duns Scotus was a medieval Scottish philosopher; 'dunce' comes from his name. Dunsinane is the hill in Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunsinane is the Scottish hill in Perthshire where Macbeth meets his end.

clue.text: Cost of purée ingredients?

indicators.note: the ingredients of the word are its letters, to be mixed into a new dish

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the makings of a purée cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients' rearranges the letters of PUREE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of India, so it measures cost or price.

clue.text: Paper whose removal might cause tears

definitions.text: Paper whose removal might cause tears

parts.words: Paper whose removal might cause tears
parts.note: a thin translucent writing paper, also read as the papery outer layer of a bulb whose peeling makes the eyes water

explanation.surface: Tearing off a sheet of paper might rip it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests rips in paper, but the outer layer of an onion makes you cry when peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin, glossy paper takes its name from the dry outer coat of the vegetable that makes cooks weep.

clue.text: To be frank, publishers are divided about women extremists

indicators.note: the publishers' letters split apart to wrap around the other piece

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press, a well-known publisher

indicators.note: extremists asks for the outermost letters of women, its first and last

explanation.surface: Publishers quarrel over feminist radicals, speaking candidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are divided about' splits the publisher to wrap the outer letters of 'women'. Oxford University Press is a standard crossword publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess or admit something openly is to be frank about it.

clue.text: Salad served in Burlington House?

parts.note: Burlington House in London is the home of the Royal Academy, RA
what is served at a meal is a dish

explanation.surface: A salad is on the menu at a grand London institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads whimsically as a dish served at the RA. Burlington House, on Piccadilly, houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery red root is a classic salad vegetable.

clue.text: Sort of charge that is formally stated

definitions.meaning: electric charge is either this kind or negative
laid down explicitly, as in law that is enacted rather than natural

explanation.surface: A legal accusation is set out in formal language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a court accusation, but it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Protons carry the plus kind of electrical charge, and law expressly enacted is called this as opposed to natural law.

clue.text: This table is irregular

definitions.meaning: a small table used now and then, kept for odd jobs
happening at intervals rather than regularly

explanation.surface: A table is described as uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' suggests a wobbly table, but means now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A small side table is named for being used only now and then, and the adjective means infrequent.

clue.text: A sore spot on pelt, but it's nothing much

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places this piece after the other

parts.note: to pelt with missiles is to pepper
a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore on their skin insists it is nothing serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' looks like an animal's skin but is the verb. A peppercorn rent is a token payment, hence nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn rent is a nominal sum, so the word stands for something trivial.

clue.text: Overriding a horse — that's normal to start with

indicators.note: to start with puts this piece at the front of the word

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
a horse ridden is a mount

explanation.surface: Riding a horse is normal to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overriding' looks like riding over, but means supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is supreme, the most important.

clue.text: Excited, being close to solution

definitions.meaning: in a guessing game, a player near the right answer is told they are getting hot

explanation.surface: A solver grows animated on nearing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent or heated in feeling, and in children's guessing games the call for someone nearing the hidden object.

clue.text: Came across but interrupted, it seemed

indicators.note: one word breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them, so met
but in the sense of however is though

explanation.surface: Someone met an interruption, or so it appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted' sets one word inside the other. The answer is an archaic poetic form meaning it seemed to me, as in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic verb means it appeared to me, an old poetic form.

clue.text: Enter old resort, so reminiscent

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Visiting an old holiday resort brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a seaside place, but as re-sort it rearranges ENTER OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redolent evokes or suggests memories, a synonym.

clue.text: Three foot coppers

definitions.meaning: police, as in Scotland ..., London's police headquarters

explanation.surface: Three police officers on foot patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' suggests walking coppers on the beat, but it is the unit of length. Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty-six inches make this imperial unit, and Scotland Yard is shorthand for the London police force.

clue.text: Birth of dwarf quite an occasion

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White
a notable occasion is an event

explanation.surface: The arrival of a small baby is a big celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a cosy euphemism for the arrival of a new baby.

clue.text: Stain on reputation to get drunk

parts.note: a blot is a mark on one's good name

explanation.surface: A scandal drives someone to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is slang for very intoxicated.

clue.text: Such bloom displayed by Mlle Gautier

definitions.text: Such bloom displayed by Mlle Gautier

parts.words: Such bloom displayed by Mlle Gautier
parts.note: Marguerite Gautier is the heroine of the Dumas novel La Dame aux Camelias, who carries a particular white flower

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman wears a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Marguerite Gautier, the courtesan of Dumas's novel and Verdi's La Traviata, is known by the flower she wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Dumas's novel is named the Lady of the Camelias for the flowering shrub's blossoms she always carries.

clue.text: Workers in distress

parts.note: people who carve or chop material into pieces, read also as feeling deeply upset

explanation.surface: Employees are in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as workers who cut things up, and also means upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut up is to be distressed or upset, while workers who cut things up chop them into pieces.

clue.text: Get something to eat, darn it

definitions.meaning: a hole worn in a sock is jokingly called by the name of this tuber, and darning mends it

explanation.surface: An exasperated cook curses while fetching food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darn it' looks like a mild oath, but means what you darn: a hole in a sock, which British slang calls a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a staple food, and a big hole in a sock is jokingly named after the lumpy tuber.

clue.text: An away team?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
a team is a side

explanation.surface: Is this the visiting team?
explanation.walkthrough: 'away team' suggests football, but 'away' is the definition, between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aside means away to one side, out of the way.

clue.text: With which to fix railway notice?

parts.note: BR is British Rail
an ad is an advertisement notice

explanation.surface: Something to pin up a railway poster.
explanation.walkthrough: A brad is a small thin nail. BR, British Rail, was the national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a slender nail with a small head, a fixing.

clue.text: Credit is tied up, we're told

indicators.note: we are told signals a word heard in speech rather than seen

parts.note: bound up like a chicken for roasting is trussed

explanation.surface: Someone says their credit is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' makes TRUSSED, bound, sound like the answer. 'tied up' suggests money locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means belief or confidence in someone, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Two sea creatures make a baby

parts.note: the nurse shark is a sea creature
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Two marine animals breed young.
explanation.definitionFit: A child being suckled or cared for is a nursling, an infant.

clue.text: Man played drums and followed the beat

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
a drummer plays a roll, so rolled

explanation.surface: A drummer kept time with the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks musical, but it is a police officer's regular round.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman walking his beat goes round it on patrol.

clue.text: Not on New Jersey town council

indicators.note: Not tells us to take away the following word, on, from the town's name

parts.note: Trenton is the capital of New Jersey

explanation.surface: A New Jersey town council is not in session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'council' seems part of the town's council, but alone it is the definition: the Council of Trent, a sixteenth-century Church gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Church's sixteenth-century Counter-Reformation assembly met in the Italian city of Trent.
